iconicAnchor.label: American Type Founders Garamond specimen pages, 1923
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: American Type Founders and commercial type-foundry specimen publishing
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The ATF specimen is a primary artifact showing how a foundry names, displays, compares, and sells a type family through coordinated title pages, alphabets, sizes, weights, and text settings.

sources.title: Warshaw Collection of Business Americana: Printing
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
supports: The collection guide documents typefounders, printers, printing specimens, trade catalogs, and related business ephemera as a coherent historical field.
It grounds specimen books in commercial and technical print practice rather than generic typographic posters.

sources.title: ATF 1923 Garamond specimen page 22b
supports: The file presents a primary specimen page with labeled display and setting evidence for a real type family.
Its scan supports the use of systematic comparison, not just a single oversized glyph.

sources.title: ATF 1923 Garamond specimen title page
supports: The title page demonstrates specimen identity and display hierarchy as part of a larger coordinated publication.
Together with an interior page, it supports cover-to-system continuity.

bundledReferenceRationale: The lead and support are excellent, complementary specimen spreads. Together they show alphabet and numeral coverage, weights, sizes, glyph anatomy, punctuation, metrics, spacing, and text settings in a systematic comparison. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/type-specimen-book/generated-lead.jpg. Distinct supporting role: Complementary support; adds a distinct subject, framing, or application without duplicating the lead.
